sections.html:
Deed and official records for Leon County are online. The County Clerk's office in Centerville also has eight public search stations, and staff will show you how the indexes work, though you are welcome to do your own research.

Find the office on the first floor of 155 North Cass Street, Centerville, TX 75833. Visitors follow a few rules:

  • No photographs of the large Tobin maps or of images on the public stations, and no flash photography.
  • Carrying a document, page or volume out of the office is a state jail felony (Penal Code 32.47).
  • Staff give no legal advice, do not decide who owns surface or mineral rights, and do not run lien searches.
  • The clerk is not required to search the records for you or vouch for their contents.

sections.h2: Office hours, filing cutoff and fees
sections.html:
Doors are open from 7:45 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. on weekdays, with no break at lunch, yet recording stops at 4 p.m. A paper that comes in after that waits for the next business day. You can pay with cash, a check or a major credit card.

Posted charges: $15 for the first page of an instrument and $4 for every page beyond it, a schedule effective January 1, 2024. E-filing into the official records goes through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. Because fees change, ask staff to verify the amount before you pay.

Work is divided among deputies. The chief deputy takes general recording, indexing and copy requests; probate, civil filings, marriage licenses and vital records each have a separate staff member and phone option. Open a call by saying you want to record a deed. Remember that clerks are not attorneys and cannot advise on what must be filed.

sections.h2: What Texas requires before a deed is recorded
sections.html:
A land conveyance can be recorded only after the owner signs it and either swears to it or acknowledges it, before two witnesses or before an officer such as a notary, county clerk, district clerk or county court judge (Property Code 12.001(b)).

The deed records hold warranty deeds of both kinds, quitclaims, trustee's, sheriff's and tax deeds, along with lien releases, affidavits and sale contracts. State law starts the fee at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, then clerk charges are added, and leaving out the grantee's mailing address can cost another $25. Pay the amount Leon County posts. Before you drive to Centerville, check the online index to confirm you have the right owner name, and bring the original signed and acknowledged deed with you.

Nobody can edit an old deed to name heirs. When an owner dies, the paper depends on the situation: an executor's or administrator's deed if the estate was administered, a court order plus the will for a muniment of title, or an affidavit of heirship as the last resort.

Leon County is rural, on Interstate 45 between Dallas and Houston. The county counts 16,894 people, a 7.2 percent rise since 2020, and 9,255 housing units. Roughly 76.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, at a middle value of $186,400. Owners with a mortgage pay about $1,557 a month, owners without one $502, and renters $907. Older residents make up 27.9 percent of the population, so estates are common: a parent's name often stays on the deed for years.

sections.h2: Who handles values and tax bills
sections.html:
Two offices split the job. The Leon Central Appraisal District sets values and the county tax assessor-collector issues bills. If your account needs a change or you question a value, contact the district at 141 W. St. Mary's, Centerville, TX 75833, telephone 903-536-2252.

Collection firms chase delinquent accounts for each taxing unit. One Waco firm covers the county, a Corsicana firm covers Normangee ISD, and a Tyler firm covers Buffalo ISD, the City of Marquez and Oakwood ISD. If a collection letter shows up, the unit that sent it tells you which firm to contact.

Statewide, the valuation date is January 1, bills land in October, and the penalty-free window closes January 31. A tax lien takes hold every January 1, so a Leon County house enters any sale still owing that year's tax. Our Leon County property tax guide covers the tax office itself.

To protest a value, write to the review board by the later of May 15 or the 30th day after delivery of your notice.

sections.h2: Title problems in the Leon County records
sections.html:
The commonest one is an estate nobody opened. Where 27.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, a parent's name often remains the last owner of record, and the file then needs a legal path to the heirs.

  • A will is normally probated within four years of death, though a judge can take a late filing when the reason is acceptable.
  • A small estate affidavit fits when there is no will, no administration pending, and assets of $75,000 or less excluding homestead and exempt property, with every heir in agreement. Two disinterested witnesses swear to it, and the death must be at least 30 days old.
  • A muniment of title allows a will to prove ownership when real estate liens are the only debts.
  • Heirs may file a sworn heirship statement with the Leon County Clerk, but a buyer or lender is free to ignore it.

An heir seeking a homestead exemption without appearing on a recorded deed supplies the appraisal district with three papers: a sworn statement of interest, a death certificate and a current utility bill.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Leon County house with a title or lien problem?
sections.html:
Yes. A cash buyer can purchase the house as it stands, and the closing agent settles recorded items wherever a payoff is documented. If you found an unreleased mortgage, a probate gap or a back tax bill in the Leon County records, send us the details and we will outline the likely route to closing.

To make that first conversation useful, gather the owner names, the date of any death, the lender on any old loan and your latest tax statement. Write down the volume and page or instrument number for each record you found, so the closing agent can pull the exact copies. The closing agent will use those to line up releases, payoffs and any estate paperwork before the day funds move.

faqs.q: What is the last hour to file a document in Leon County?
faqs.a: Recording ends at 4 p.m., although the office stays open until 4:45 p.m. on weekdays. Papers that arrive later are handled the following business day.

faqs.q: What fee applies to filing a deed with the Leon County Clerk?
faqs.a: The clerk lists $15 for page one and $4 for every added page of an instrument, effective January 1, 2024. Ask the office to confirm the amount when you file.

faqs.q: Are Leon County deed records available online?
faqs.a: Yes. Deed and official records are online, and the same records back to 1828 can be viewed on public stations in the Centerville office.

faqs.q: Will the Leon County Clerk tell me who owns the minerals?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot determine surface or mineral ownership or run lien searches, so that work falls to a closing agent or a lawyer.

faqs.q: Where do I contest a Leon County appraisal?
faqs.a: Call the Leon Central Appraisal District at 903-536-2252. Written protests to the review board are due on the later of May 15 and the 30th day after delivery of the value notice.
